title.raw: 卷119 志九十四 职官六

translations.literal: Treatise Ninety-Four
translations.idiomatic: Treatise Ninety-Four

translations.literal: Offices Six: The New Official System
translations.idiomatic: Offices Six: The New Official System

sentences.zh: 內閣外務部出使大臣稅務處民政部內外巡警總廳度支部清理財政處大清銀行

translations.literal: Grand Secretariat; Ministry of Foreign Affairs; envoys abroad; Customs Office; Ministry of Civil Affairs; Inner and Outer Metropolitan Police Headquarters; Ministry of Revenue; Office for the Settlement of Public Accounts; Imperial Bank of China
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, envoys abroad, Customs Office, Ministry of Civil Affairs, Inner and Outer Metropolitan Police Headquarters, Ministry of Revenue, Office for the Settlement of Public Accounts, and Imperial Bank of China

sentences.zh: 造幣總廠學部國子監大學堂陸軍部海軍部法部修訂法律館大理院

translations.literal: General Mint; Ministry of Education; Directorate of Education; Imperial University; Army Ministry; Navy Ministry; Ministry of Justice; Law Revision Bureau; Supreme Court of Justice
translations.idiomatic: The General Mint, Ministry of Education, Directorate of Education, Imperial University, Army Ministry, Navy Ministry, Ministry of Justice, Law Revision Bureau, and Supreme Court of Justice

sentences.zh: 京師各級審檢廳農工商部郵傳部軍諮府弼德院資政院鹽政院

translations.literal: Capital courts and procuratorates at all levels; Ministry of Agriculture, Industry, and Commerce; Ministry of Posts and Communications; Military Advisory Council; Council of State; Political Consultative Council; Salt Administration
translations.idiomatic: Capital trial and procuratorate offices at all levels, the Ministry of Agriculture, Industry, and Commerce, Ministry of Posts and Communications, Military Advisory Council, Council of State, Political Consultative Council, and Salt Administration

sentences.zh: 典禮院禮學館提學使提法使外省各級審檢廳東三省各司禁衛軍

translations.literal: Court of Rites; Institute of Ritual Learning; provincial education commissioners; provincial judicial commissioners; provincial courts and procuratorates; the three eastern provinces' departments; Imperial Guard
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Rites, Institute of Ritual Learning, provincial education and judicial commissioners, provincial courts and procuratorates, departments of the three eastern provinces, and the Imperial Guard

sentences.zh: 督練公所軍制鎮制陸軍鎮監巡防隊海軍艦制

translations.literal: Provincial Training Offices; army organization; division organization; army division prisons; patrol forces; naval ship organization
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Training Offices, army and division organization, army division prisons, patrol forces, and naval ship organization

sentences.zh: 清初釐定官制，職儀粗具。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qing, the official system was fixed and duties and ceremonial forms were roughly in place.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qing the official system was established and its duties and ceremonial forms were roughly in place.

sentences.zh: 中更六七作，存改洄沿，世不同矣。

translations.literal: It underwent six or seven revisions; what was kept, changed, or carried over differed from age to age.
translations.idiomatic: It was revised six or seven times, with institutions kept, altered, or carried forward so that no two eras were quite alike.

sentences.zh: 延及德宗，外患躡跡，譯署始立。

translations.literal: Down to the Guangxu Emperor, foreign troubles followed close upon one another, and the Translation Office was first established.
translations.idiomatic: By the Guangxu reign foreign crises came in quick succession, and the Translation Office was first established.

sentences.zh: 繼改專部，商、警、學部接踵而設，並省府、寺，乃分十部。

translations.literal: Later it was changed to a dedicated ministry; the Commerce, Police, and Education ministries were set up in turn; provincial offices and courts were consolidated, and there were ten ministries.
translations.idiomatic: It later became a dedicated ministry; Commerce, Police, and Education ministries followed; provincial offices and courts were consolidated into ten ministries.

sentences.zh: 嗣議立憲，理籓改部，軍諮設處，復更巡警為民政，戶為度支，商為農工商，兵為陸軍，附立海軍處，刑為法，別立大理院，又取工部所司輪路郵電專設郵傳部。

translations.literal: When constitutional government was discussed, the Court of Colonial Affairs became a ministry, a Military Advisory office was set up, patrol police became civil affairs, Revenue became finance, Commerce became agriculture, industry, and commerce, War became the army with a naval office attached, Punishments became justice with a separate Supreme Court, and the Works Ministry's railways, posts, and telegraphs went to a new Posts and Communications Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Constitutional plans brought a Colonial Affairs ministry, a Military Advisory office, and renamed ministries: Civil Affairs, Finance, Agriculture-Industry-Commerce, Army (with a naval office), Justice (with a separate Supreme Court), and Posts and Communications split from Works.

translations.literal: Comparing the present with the past, the institutions were indeed numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with earlier times, the institutions had become remarkably numerous.

sentences.zh: 宣統紹述，合樞於閣，增海軍部，省吏部，改禮部為典禮院，鹽政處為鹽政院。

translations.literal: The Xuantong reign continued the reform: the Grand Council was merged into the cabinet, a Navy Ministry was added, the Board of Civil Appointments was abolished, the Board of Rites became the Court of Rites, and the Salt Office became the Salt Administration.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuantong reforms merged the Grand Council into the cabinet, added a Navy Ministry, abolished the Board of Civil Appointments, made the Board of Rites a Court of Rites, and elevated the Salt Office to a Salt Administration.

sentences.zh: 猶慮閣權過重，設弼德院以相維繫，資政院以為監督。

translations.literal: Still fearing excessive cabinet power, the Council of State was set up to balance it and the Political Consultative Council to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing an overpowerful cabinet, the Council of State was added as a counterweight and the Political Consultative Council as a supervisory body.

sentences.zh: 增埤前事，取臬殊方，因事創名，官冗職雜，階資官品，肇域未區。

translations.literal: Building on earlier matters, drawing on various regions, offices were created ad hoc by the affair; posts were redundant and duties mixed; grades and ranks were not yet clearly demarcated.
translations.idiomatic: Building on past practice and borrowing from many regions, ad hoc offices multiplied; posts overlapped, duties blurred, and ranks were not yet clearly sorted.

sentences.zh: 簡奏咨補，故實斯在，輯而存之，具載後簡，亦得失之林也。

translations.literal: Imperial selection, memorial appointment, and consultative appointment preserve the facts; compiled and preserved here in detail below, this is also a record of gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial selection, memorial appointment, and consultative appointment are recorded here in full below—a forest of what worked and what did not.

sentences.zh: 內閣總理大臣，協理大臣，各一人。

translations.literal: Cabinet: one Prime Minister and one Assistant Prime Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The cabinet had one prime minister and one assistant prime minister.

translations.literal: Specially selected by imperial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Both were specially selected by imperial appointment.

translations.literal: Ten State Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: There were ten state ministers.

translations.literal: Filled concurrently by the ministers of the departments.
translations.idiomatic: They were filled concurrently by the various ministry heads.

translations.literal: One Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: There was one chancellor.

translations.literal: Proclamation Bureau □□ Director and Deputy □ Director, one each.
translations.idiomatic: The Proclamation Bureau had one director and one deputy director.

sentences.zh: 制諮、敘官、統計、印鑄四局，局長各一人。

translations.literal: Four bureaus—Drafting, Personnel Records, Statistics, and Seals—each with one director.
translations.idiomatic: Four bureaus—Drafting, Personnel Records, Statistics, and Seals—each had one director.

translations.literal: From the Chancellor downward, all were appointed by imperial selection upon request.
translations.idiomatic: From the chancellor downward, all were appointed by imperial selection upon request.

sentences.zh: 其屬有：僉事，印鑄藝師，俱奏補。

translations.literal: Subordinates included: secretaries and seal-casting master artisans, all appointed by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates included secretaries and seal-casting master artisans, all appointed by memorial.

translations.literal: Artisans and record clerks were all appointed by consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Artisans and record clerks were appointed by consultation.

translations.literal: Various posts.
translations.idiomatic: Various posts.

sentences.zh: 所轄法制院，院長，副院長，各一人。

translations.literal: Under its jurisdiction, the Legislative Drafting Court: one president and one vice president.
translations.idiomatic: It oversaw the Legislative Drafting Court, with one president and one vice president.

translations.literal: Four Counsellors.
translations.idiomatic: There were four counsellors.

translations.literal: All appointed by imperial selection upon request.
translations.idiomatic: All were appointed by imperial selection upon request.

translations.literal: Counsellor-assistants, appointed by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Counsellor-assistants were appointed by memorial.

sentences.zh: 僉事，錄事，視事繁簡酌置。

translations.literal: Secretaries and record clerks were placed according to the weight of business.
translations.idiomatic: Secretaries and record clerks were assigned according to workload.

sentences.zh: 總理掌參畫機要，締綸時務。

translations.literal: The Prime Minister managed planning of state secrets and drafting of timely policy.
translations.idiomatic: The prime minister planned state secrets and drafted timely policy.

sentences.zh: 法律詔令，會國務大臣尾署名銜。

translations.literal: For laws and edicts, State Ministers countersigned at the end.
translations.idiomatic: Laws and edicts bore the countersignatures of the state ministers at the end.

sentences.zh: 事涉一部或數部，會所司大臣署之。

translations.literal: Matters involving one or several ministries were signed by the responsible ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Matters touching one or more ministries were signed by the responsible ministers.

sentences.zh: 會議時充議長，協理佐之。

translations.literal: At meetings he served as chair; the Assistant Prime Minister assisted.
translations.idiomatic: In council he chaired meetings; the assistant prime minister assisted.

sentences.zh: 丞掌主閣務，綜領眾局，方軌諸長。

translations.literal: The Chancellor directed cabinet affairs, oversaw all bureaus, and kept the bureau chiefs in line.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor ran cabinet affairs, oversaw all bureaus, and coordinated the bureau chiefs.

sentences.zh: 承宣掌布絲綸，守法典，司文書圖籍。

translations.literal: The Proclamation Bureau issued imperial rescripts, upheld the legal canon, and managed documents and archives.
translations.idiomatic: The Proclamation Bureau issued rescripts, upheld the legal canon, and managed documents and archives.

sentences.zh: 制誥掌詔旨制敕，璽書冊命，起草進畫，稽頒寶星勳章，典領籓封勳級。

translations.literal: Drafting managed edicts, patent letters, and commissions; drafted and presented for approval; audited award of orders and medals; and directed enfeoffment ranks for the domains.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting handled edicts, sealed commissions, and drafts for imperial approval; it audited orders and medals and managed noble ranks for the domains.

sentences.zh: 敘官掌考功定課，匯覈履行。

translations.literal: Personnel Records managed merit evaluation and fixed assessments, compiling and verifying fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel Records evaluated merit, fixed assessments, and verified fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 統計掌統一計表，刊行年鑒。

translations.literal: Statistics compiled unified statistical tables and published yearbooks.
translations.idiomatic: Statistics compiled unified tables and published yearbooks.

translations.literal: Seals edited the Official Gazette.
translations.idiomatic: The Seals Bureau edited the Official Gazette.

translations.literal: The rest followed the former system.
translations.idiomatic: The rest followed the former system.

translations.literal: See the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: See the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 法制院掌編纂法規，修明法令，擬上候裁。

translations.literal: The Legislative Drafting Court compiled regulations, clarified laws, and drafted submissions for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: The Legislative Drafting Court compiled regulations, clarified statutes, and submitted drafts for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十二年，改組內閣，設會議政務處，以各部尚書為內閣政務大臣。

translations.literal: In Guangxu 32 the cabinet was reorganized; a Council of Government Affairs was set up, with each ministry head as a cabinet affairs minister.
translations.idiomatic: In 1906 the cabinet was reorganized with a Council of Government Affairs whose members were the ministry heads.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，改責任內閣，以軍機大臣為總、協理大臣，並定內閣屬官制。

translations.literal: In Xuantong 3 a responsible cabinet was instituted; Grand Councilors became Prime and Assistant Prime Ministers, and subordinate cabinet offices were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1911 a responsible cabinet was formed from Grand Councilors as prime and assistant prime ministers, with subordinate offices as listed.

translations.literal: As listed above.
translations.idiomatic: As listed above.

sentences.zh: 外務部外務大臣，副大臣，各一人。

translations.literal: Ministry of Foreign Affairs: one minister and one vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs had one minister and one vice minister.

translations.literal: Specially selected by imperial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Both were specially selected.

sentences.zh: 承政□左、右丞，參議□左、右參議，各一人。

translations.literal: Directorate of Administration [□]: one left and one right vice director; Counselling [□]: one left and one right counsellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate had left and right vice directors; the Counselling office had left and right counsellors—one each.

translations.literal: All appointed by imperial selection upon request.
translations.idiomatic: All were appointed by imperial selection upon request.

translations.literal: Four counsellor-assistants.
translations.idiomatic: There were four counsellor-assistants.

translations.literal: Appointed by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: They were appointed by memorial.

translations.literal: Subordinates: two office clerks of the General Affairs [□] office.
translations.idiomatic: It had two general-affairs office clerks.

translations.literal: Appointed by consultation.
translations.idiomatic: They were appointed by consultation.

sentences.zh: 和會、考工、榷算、庶務四司，郎中、員外郎、主事各二人。

translations.literal: Four departments—Protocol, Engineering, Tariffs, and General Affairs—each with two bureau directors, two vice directors, and two section chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Four departments—Protocol, Engineering, Tariffs, and General Affairs—each had two directors, vice directors, and section chiefs.

translations.literal: All appointed by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: All were appointed by memorial.

translations.literal: The same for all ministries above.
translations.idiomatic: The same pattern applied to all ministries above.

sentences.zh: 大臣掌主交涉，昭布德信，保護僑人傭客，以慎邦交。

translations.literal: The minister directed negotiations, spread imperial virtue and trust, and protected overseas Chinese and laborers to safeguard foreign relations.
translations.idiomatic: The minister directed diplomacy, displayed imperial virtue, and protected overseas Chinese and laborers.

translations.literal: The vice minister assisted.
translations.idiomatic: The vice minister assisted.

sentences.zh: 丞掌機密文移，綜領眾務。

translations.literal: The vice director managed confidential documents and oversaw all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The vice director handled confidential papers and oversaw all affairs.

sentences.zh: 參議掌審議法令，參事佐之。

translations.literal: Counsellors reviewed laws; counsellor-assistants assisted.
translations.idiomatic: Counsellors reviewed laws; counsellor-assistants assisted.

translations.literal: The same in all ministries.
translations.idiomatic: The same in all ministries.

sentences.zh: 和會掌使臣覲見，盟約賞賚，兼司領事更替，司員敘遷。

translations.literal: Protocol managed envoys' audiences, treaty gifts, consular changes, and staff promotions.
translations.idiomatic: Protocol managed audiences, treaty gifts, consular rotation, and staff promotions.

sentences.zh: 考工掌司鐵軌、礦產、電線、船政，凡製造軍火，聘用客卿，招工、遊學諸事，各擅其職。

translations.literal: Engineering managed railways, mines, telegraph lines, and naval affairs, including ordnance manufacture, foreign advisers, labor recruitment, and study abroad—each with its duty.
translations.idiomatic: Engineering managed railways, mines, telegraphs, shipbuilding, ordnance, foreign advisers, labor, and study abroad.

sentences.zh: 榷算掌蕃貨海舶征榷貿易，綜典國債、郵政，勾檢本部暨出使度支。

translations.literal: Tariffs managed foreign goods, maritime trade levies, public debt, and postal affairs, and audited ministry and legation accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Tariffs managed foreign trade levies, public debt, and post, and audited ministry and legation finances.

sentences.zh: 度務掌江海防務，疆域界址，凡傳教、遊歷，賞恤、禁令，裁判獄訟，並按約以待。

translations.literal: General Affairs managed coastal defense, boundaries, missionary travel, rewards and bans, and judicial cases under treaty.
translations.idiomatic: General Affairs handled coastal defense, boundaries, missionary travel, rewards and prohibitions, and treaty-based litigation.

sentences.zh: 有丞、參上行走，額外司員，七品小京官。

translations.literal: There were vice directors and counsellors on active duty, supernumerary staff, and seventh-rank junior capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: Active vice directors and counsellors, supernumerary staff, and seventh-rank junior capital officials served on detail.

sentences.zh: 民政、郵傳、法部小京官定額缺。

translations.literal: Fixed quotas of junior capital officials existed in Civil Affairs, Posts and Communications, and Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Civil Affairs, Posts and Communications, and Justice had fixed quotas of junior capital officials.

sentences.zh: 所轄：儲材館，提調、幫提調各一人。

translations.literal: Under jurisdiction: the Talent Repository, one chief coordinator and one assistant coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: It oversaw the Talent Repository with one chief and one assistant coordinator.

translations.literal: Selected from ministry staff.
translations.idiomatic: They were chosen from ministry staff.

sentences.zh: 文案、支應、庶務、俱派員分治其事。

translations.literal: Documentation, supplies, and general affairs each had assigned officers.
translations.idiomatic: Documentation, supplies, and general affairs each had assigned officers.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，定恰克圖市約，置辦理俄事大臣，見第五款。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 5 the Kyakhta market treaty was fixed and a commissioner for Russian affairs was appointed; see item five.
translations.idiomatic: In 1727 the Kyakhta treaty was concluded and a commissioner for Russian affairs appointed; see item five.

translations.literal: Not a permanent post.
translations.idiomatic: It was not a permanent post.

translations.literal: In Xianfeng 1 it was transferred to the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 it passed to the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 十年，文宗北狩，特置專官辦理撫局。

translations.literal: In year 10, when the Xianfeng Emperor went north, a dedicated officer was appointed to handle negotiations.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, when the Xianfeng Emperor fled north, a dedicated negotiator was appointed.

sentences.zh: 其冬，設總理各國事務衙門，命恭親王奕訢領之。

translations.literal: That winter the Zongli Yamen was established, with Prince Gong Yixin placed in charge.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Zongli Yamen was founded under Prince Gong Yixin.

sentences.zh: 司員統稱章京，置滿、漢各八人。

translations.literal: Staff were called zhangjing; eight Manchu and eight Han were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Staff were titled zhangjing—eight Manchu and eight Han.

translations.literal: At the time a system of divided offices handling affairs was used.
translations.idiomatic: A divided-office system was then in use.

sentences.zh: 戶部司員覈關稅，理籓部司員典文移，兵部司員治台站驛遞，內閣人員主機密，俱隸總辦、幫辦。

translations.literal: Revenue staff audited customs; Colonial Affairs staff managed documents; War staff handled courier stations; Grand Secretariat staff handled secrets—all under chief and assistant managers.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue, Colonial Affairs, War, and Grand Secretariat staff handled customs, documents, couriers, and secrets under chief and assistant managers.

sentences.zh: 三年，改為英、法、俄、美四股。

translations.literal: In year 3 it was reorganized into four sections: Britain, France, Russia, and the United States.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 it was divided into British, French, Russian, and American sections.

translations.literal: In year 9 a Coastal Defense section was added.
translations.idiomatic: In 1869 a Coastal Defense section was added.

sentences.zh: 後改俄、德、英、法、日本五股。

translations.literal: Later changed to five sections: Russia, Germany, Britain, France, and Japan.
translations.idiomatic: It later became five sections: Russia, Germany, Britain, France, and Japan.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，合俄、德為一，增設秘書、機要二股。

translations.literal: In Xuantong 1 Russia and Germany were merged and Secretariat and Secret Affairs sections were added.
translations.idiomatic: In 1909 Russia and Germany were merged and Secretariat and Secret Affairs sections added.

sentences.zh: 明年，置總辦四人，曰總辦章京。

translations.literal: The next year four chief managers were appointed, called chief zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: The next year four chief managers called chief zhangjing were appointed.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，增置額外章京，滿、漢各二人。

translations.literal: In Tongzhi 1 supernumerary zhangjing were added—two Manchu and two Han.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 two supernumerary Manchu and two Han zhangjing were added.

translations.literal: In year 2 six more were added for each.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 six more were added for each.

translations.literal: In Guangxu 9 four more were added for each.
translations.idiomatic: In 1883 four more were added for each.

translations.literal: In year 10 four were cut from each.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884 four were cut from each.

translations.literal: In year 23 two more were added for each.
translations.idiomatic: In 1897 two more were added for each.

sentences.zh: 三年，設司務□，置司務二人。

translations.literal: In year 3 the General Affairs [□] office was set up with two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 a general-affairs office was set up with two clerks.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十七年，辛丑和約成，更名外務部，班列各部上。

translations.literal: In Guangxu 27, after the Boxer Protocol, it was renamed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and ranked above other ministries.
translations.idiomatic: In 1901, after the Boxer Protocol, it became the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, ranked above other ministries.

sentences.zh: 置總理親王，會辦尚書，兼會辦左、右侍郎，各一人；

translations.literal: One supervising prince, one co-managing minister, and one left and one right co-managing vice minister were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: A supervising prince, co-managing minister, and left and right co-managing vice ministers were appointed.

sentences.zh: 改總辦為左、右丞，左、右參議各一人。

translations.literal: Chief managers became left and right vice directors; one left and one right counsellor were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Chief managers became left and right vice directors with left and right counsellors.

sentences.zh: 並置郎中以次各官，不分滿、漢。

translations.literal: Bureau directors and subordinate posts were established without Manchu-Han distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Directors and subordinates were appointed without Manchu-Han distinction.

sentences.zh: 三十二年改訂官制，意合滿、漢，而翰林、都察兩院仍依往制。

translations.literal: In year 32 the official system was revised to unite Manchu and Han, but the Hanlin Academy and Censorate kept the old rules.
translations.idiomatic: The 1906 reform aimed to unite Manchu and Han, but the Hanlin Academy and Censorate kept old rules.

sentences.zh: 是歲增置繙譯官十有五人。

translations.literal: That year fifteen translators were added.
translations.idiomatic: That year fifteen translators were added.

sentences.zh: 七、八、九品各五人，分股治事。

translations.literal: Five each of the seventh, eighth, and ninth ranks, divided among sections.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen translators of the seventh through ninth ranks served in the sections.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，新內閣成，省總理、會辦兼職，改尚書為大臣，侍郎為副大臣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong, the new cabinet was formed; the concurrent posts of director-general and co-director were abolished, ministers (shangshu) were renamed grand ministers (dachen), and vice ministers (shilang) were renamed deputy grand ministers (fu dachen).
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuantong (1911), the new cabinet took shape: the old concurrent titles of director-general and co-director were dropped, ministers became grand ministers, and vice ministers became deputy grand ministers.

translations.literal: One vice-minister post was abolished in each ministry; all ministries were alike.
translations.idiomatic: Each ministry likewise shed one vice-minister post.

translations.literal: The system of supervising ministries was abolished at this point.
translations.idiomatic: With that, the practice of assigning overseers to run the ministries came to an end.

translations.literal: First-rank envoy ministers held rank 1a.
translations.idiomatic: First-class envoys held the top civil rank, 1a.

translations.literal: They were specially selected by imperial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: They were specially selected by imperial appointment.

translations.literal: Counselors held rank 3a.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors held rank 3a.

translations.literal: Interpreters held rank 5a.
translations.idiomatic: Interpreters held rank 5a.

translations.literal: All were appointed by memorial to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: All were appointed by memorial to the throne.

translations.idiomatic: In early Kangxi, Russian missions came and went, but no standing system yet existed.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，始遣使辦理交涉，以道員志剛等及美使蒲安臣膺其選。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tongzhi, envoys were first dispatched to handle negotiations; circuit intendant Zhigang and others, and the American minister Burlingame, were chosen.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 6 (1867), the court first sent envoys to handle diplomacy; Zhigang, a circuit intendant, and the American minister Anson Burlingame were among those chosen.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，定出使制，命侍郎郭嵩燾使英，翰林院侍講何如璋使日本，京卿陳蘭彬使美日秘國，俱置副使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu the envoy system was fixed; Vice Minister Guo Songtao was sent to Britain, Hanlin expositor He Ruzhang to Japan, and capital official Chen Lanbin to the United States, Japan, and Peru, each with a deputy envoy.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 1 (1875), the permanent envoy system was established: Vice Minister Guo Songtao to Britain, Hanlin expositor He Ruzhang to Japan, and capital official Chen Lanbin to the United States, Japan, and Peru—each with a deputy.

sentences.zh: 別設秘、日分館，置金山、嘉裡約、古巴各總領事。

translations.literal: Separate branch legations were set up for Peru and Japan, and consuls-general were placed at San Francisco, Rio de Janeiro, and Cuba.
translations.idiomatic: Branch legations were opened for Peru and Japan, with consuls-general at San Francisco, Rio, and Cuba.

translations.literal: Later, when they became sovereign states, ministers plenipotentiary were sent instead.
translations.idiomatic: When those countries were recognized as fully sovereign, the court began sending ministers plenipotentiary.

sentences.zh: 二年，定使館參贊二人，絲番譯四人。

translations.literal: In the second year, two legation counselors and four silk-bureau translators were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 2, each legation was allotted two counselors and four silk-bureau translators.

sentences.zh: 十四年，復定繙譯、隨員二人或三人。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, translators and attachés were again fixed at two or three.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 14, the quota for translators and attachés was reset at two or three.

sentences.zh: 分館參贊兼領事一人，絲番譯、隨員各一人，參贊如故。

translations.literal: Each branch legation had one counselor also serving as consul, one silk-bureau translator, and one attaché; counselors remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Each branch had one counselor-consul, one silk-bureau translator, and one attaché, while full legations kept their counselors.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，定參贊以次各員額，如前所列。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year the quotas for counselors and subordinate posts were fixed as listed above.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 32, staff quotas from counselor downward were fixed as listed above.

sentences.zh: 厥後聯翩四出，英使兼領義、比，俄使兼駐德，以奧、和隸之。

translations.literal: Thereafter envoys were dispatched in quick succession; the British minister also supervised Italy and Belgium, the Russian minister was also stationed in Germany, and Austria and the Netherlands were subordinated to them.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys then fanned out abroad: the British minister also covered Italy and Belgium; the Russian minister was also posted to Germany, with Austria and the Netherlands under that legation.

sentences.zh: 四年，置新嘉坡領事，後改總領事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year a consul was placed at Singapore, later changed to consul-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 4 a consul was posted to Singapore, later upgraded to consul-general.

translations.literal: Superintendent officials were placed at various Japanese ports.
translations.idiomatic: Superintendent officials were posted to Japanese treaty ports.

translations.literal: Later they were changed to consuls.
translations.idiomatic: They were later retitled consuls.

sentences.zh: 明年，省副使，置檀香山領事。

translations.literal: The next year deputy envoys were abolished and a consul was placed at Honolulu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year deputy envoys were abolished and a consul opened at Honolulu.

translations.literal: In the eighth year a consul was placed at New York.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 8 a consul was posted to New York.

sentences.zh: 十三年，置小呂宋總領事，仰光領事，檳榔嶼副領事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year a consul-general was placed in the Philippines, a consul at Rangoon, and a vice-consul at Penang.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 13 posts opened at Manila (consul-general), Rangoon (consul), and Penang (vice-consul).

translations.literal: Later changed to consul.
translations.idiomatic: Penang was later upgraded to consul.

sentences.zh: 十七年，置南洋各島領事。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year consuls were placed on various South Sea islands.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 17 consuls were posted across the South Seas.

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year a dedicated minister to France was specially selected.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 21 a dedicated minister to France was appointed.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，簡德國專使，和改隸之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year a dedicated minister to Germany was specially selected, and the Netherlands was subordinated to him.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 23 a dedicated minister went to Germany, and the Dutch legation was placed under him.

translations.literal: A minister to Korea was also added.
translations.idiomatic: A minister to Korea was added as well.

sentences.zh: 三十三年撤回，改總領事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was withdrawn and replaced with a consul-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 33 the Korean minister was recalled and the post became a consul-general.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，置韓國各口岸領事，及海參葳商務委員。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year consuls were placed at Korean ports and a commercial commissioner at Vladivostok.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 26 consuls opened at Korean ports and a commercial commissioner at Vladivostok.

translations.literal: Later changed to consul-general.
translations.idiomatic: Vladivostok was later upgraded to consul-general.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，改駐法使臣兼使日國，駐美使臣兼使古巴，別設分館，並簡奧、義、比三國專使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the minister in France was also to serve Japan, the minister in the United States also Cuba, with separate branch legations; dedicated ministers to Austria, Italy, and Belgium were specially selected.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 28 the French minister also covered Japan, the American minister Cuba (with branch legations), and separate ministers were appointed to Austria, Italy, and Belgium.

translations.literal: The next year a Mexican branch legation was established.
translations.idiomatic: The next year a Mexican branch legation opened.

sentences.zh: 三十年，置南斐洲總領事。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year a consul-general was placed in South Africa.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 30 a consul-general was posted to South Africa.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，簡和國專使兼理保和會事，並以法日使臣兼領葡使，尋設葡分館。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year a dedicated Dutch minister was specially selected to handle Hague Conference affairs; the French and Japanese ministers also supervised Portugal, and soon a Portuguese branch legation was set up.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 31 a Dutch minister handled Hague Peace Conference business; French and Japanese ministers briefly covered Portugal until a Portuguese branch legation opened.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，定使臣為二品專官，並參贊等官品秩。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year envoys were fixed as dedicated second-rank officials, with ranks for counselors and other posts.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 34 envoys became dedicated second-rank posts, with formal ranks for counselors and staff.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，置美利濱、坎拿大、巴拿馬總領事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong consuls-general were placed at Melbourne, Canada, and Panama.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1 consuls-general opened at Melbourne, Canada, and Panama.

sentences.zh: 嗣是澳洲、溫哥埠、薩摩島、紐絲綸諸領事踵相躡。

translations.idiomatic: Consuls at Australia, Vancouver, Samoa, and New South Wales followed in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 三年，置爪哇總領事，泗水、巴東領事。

sentences.zh: 其秋置朝鮮新義州領事。

translations.idiomatic: Four customs commissioners, six deputies, and fifty-nine station commissioners—including five at Chaozhou.

translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou, Yuezhou, and Beihai each had three.

translations.idiomatic: Senior ministry officials filled them.

translations.literal: Soon it was changed so governors-general and governors supervised them in name only.
translations.idiomatic: Later governors-general and governors nominally supervised them—largely in name.

sentences.zh: 自道光以來，海疆日辟，於是始置北洋、南洋通商大臣，關道及監督隸之。

translations.literal: Since Daoguang the maritime frontier expanded daily; then Northern and Southern Commissioners for Trade were first established, and circuit intendants and superintendents were subordinate to them.
translations.idiomatic: From the Daoguang era onward, as treaty ports multiplied, Northern and Southern Commissioners for Trade were created, with circuit intendants and superintendents under them.

translations.literal: Some were also concurrently managed by generals.
translations.idiomatic: Some ports were also overseen by generals.

sentences.zh: 津海歸直隸津海道管理，山海歸奉天奉錦山海道管理，東海歸山東登萊青道管理，俱隸北洋。

translations.literal: Tianjin maritime customs was managed by the Zhili Tianjin circuit; Shanhaiguan by the Fengtian Feng-Jin-Shan circuit; Donghai by the Shandong Deng-Lai-Qing circuit—all subordinate to the Northern Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin fell under the Zhili Tianjin circuit, Shanhaiguan under the Fengtian Feng-Jin-Shan circuit, and Donghai under Shandong's Deng-Lai-Qing circuit—all under the Northern Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鎮江歸江蘇常鎮通道管理，江海歸江蘇蘇松太道管理，蕪湖歸安徽皖南道管理，浙海歸浙江寧紹台道管理，甌海歸浙江溫處道管理，江漢歸湖北漢黃德道管理，宜昌歸湖北荊宜施道管理，重慶歸四川川東道管理，俱隸南洋。

translations.literal: Zhenjiang was managed by the Jiangsu Chang-Zhen circuit; Jianghai by the Su-Song-Tai circuit; Wuhu by the Anhui Wan-Nan circuit; Zhejiang maritime by the Ning-Shao-Tai circuit; Wenzhou by the Wen-Chu circuit; Hankou by the Han-Huang-De circuit; Yichang by the Jing-Yi-Shi circuit; Chongqing by the Sichuan Chuandong circuit—all subordinate to the Southern Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjiang, Jianghai, Wuhu, Zhejiang, Wenzhou, Hankou, Yichang, and Chongqing were managed by their respective provincial circuits—all under the Southern Commissioner.

translations.literal: Fujian maritime customs was managed by the Fuzhou general.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian customs came under the Fuzhou general.

sentences.zh: 粵海、潮海、北海、瓊海、九龍、拱北，監督各一人。

translations.literal: Guangzhou, Chaozhou, Beihai, Qionghai, Kowloon, and Gongbei each had one superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou, Chaozhou, Beihai, Qionghai, Kowloon, and Gongbei each had its own superintendent.

sentences.zh: 嘉峪歸甘肅安肅道管理，龍州歸廣西太平思順道管理，蒙自歸雲南臨安開廣道管理，隸本省督、撫。

translations.literal: Jiayu was managed by the Gansu Anxi circuit; Longzhou by the Guangxi Taiping-Sishun circuit; Mengzi by the Yunnan Lin'an-Kaiguang circuit—subordinate to the provincial governor-general and governor.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayu, Longzhou, and Mengzi fell under their provincial circuits and local governors.

sentences.zh: 咸豐以後，聘用英人威妥瑪、美人斯密斯氏襄辦稅務，李泰國繼之。

translations.literal: After Xianfeng the Englishman Wade and the American Smith were employed to assist in customs; Lay succeeded them.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianfeng, Thomas Wade and an American named Smith assisted customs work; Horatio Lay succeeded them.

translations.literal: Lay was appointed Inspector General;
translations.idiomatic: Lay was appointed Inspector General;

sentences.zh: 凡海關俱置稅務司、副稅務司，後沿江各埠，及內地陸路增開口岸，並屬海關。

translations.literal: every maritime customs station had a commissioner and deputy commissioner; later treaty ports along the rivers and inland overland ports opened additionally all belonged to customs.
translations.idiomatic: every station gained a commissioner and deputy; later river and inland treaty ports were folded into the same system.

sentences.zh: 是為海關募用客卿之始。

translations.literal: This was the beginning of employing foreign experts in customs.
translations.idiomatic: That was when customs began relying on foreign administrators.

sentences.zh: 時管轄之權屬總理衙門。

translations.literal: At that time supervisory authority belonged to the Zongli Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Authority then rested with the Zongli Yamen (Foreign Office).

sentences.zh: 光緒二十三年，始設稅務處，總稅務司以次各官並受其節度。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Guangxu the Customs Office was first established; the Inspector General and all subordinate officials were subject to its direction.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 23 the Customs Office was created, bringing the Inspector General and all subordinates under its control.

sentences.zh: 先是戶關、工關分隸戶、工兩部，至是始以常關標名。

translations.literal: Previously household customs and works customs were separately subordinate to the Ministries of Revenue and Works; at this point they were first labeled native customs stations.
translations.idiomatic: Household and works customs had belonged to the Revenue and Works ministries; now they were formally called native customs (changguan).

sentences.zh: 嗣外部與本處定常關分設稅局，五十里外者歸監督，五十里內者歸稅務司，此內、外常關名稱所由昉也。

translations.literal: Later the Foreign Ministry and this office fixed that native customs would set up tax bureaus separately: those beyond fifty li were under superintendents, within fifty li under customs commissioners—whence the names inner and outer native customs.
translations.idiomatic: The Foreign Ministry and the Customs Office later split native customs: stations beyond fifty li answered to Chinese superintendents, within fifty li to foreign commissioners—origin of the inner/outer changguan distinction.

sentences.zh: 民政大臣，副大臣，左、右丞，左、右參議，各一人。

translations.literal: Minister of Civil Affairs, deputy minister, left and right vice ministers, left and right counselors, one each.
translations.idiomatic: Minister and deputy minister of Civil Affairs, with left and right vice ministers and counselors, one each.

sentences.zh: 承政□員外郎，主事，小京官，各四人。

translations.literal: Chancellery □ bureau: four vice directors, four section chiefs, and four junior capital officials each.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellery office: four vice directors, four section chiefs, and four junior capital officials each.

translations.literal: Counselor □ bureau: two counselors (canshi).
translations.idiomatic: The Counselor office: two counselor-assistants.

sentences.zh: 民治、警政、疆裡、營繕、衛生五司，郎中八人，民治，警政、疆裡各二人，餘各一人。

translations.literal: Five bureaus—Civil Administration, Police Administration, Boundaries, Public Works, and Health—eight bureau directors: two each for Civil Administration, Police, and Boundaries; one each for the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Five bureaus—civil administration, police, boundaries, public works, and health—had eight directors: two each for civil administration, police, and boundaries; one for the others.

sentences.zh: 員外郎十有六人，民治、警政、營繕各四人，餘各二人。

translations.literal: Sixteen vice directors: four each for Civil Administration, Police, and Public Works; two each for the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen vice directors: four each for civil administration, police, and public works; two for the rest.

sentences.zh: 主事十有八人，民治、警政各五人，營繕四人，餘各二人。

translations.literal: Eighteen section chiefs: five each for Civil Administration and Police; four for Public Works; two each for the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen section chiefs: five each for civil administration and police; four for public works; two for the rest.

translations.literal: One junior capital official for each bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Each bureau had one junior capital official.

sentences.zh: 習藝所員外郎一人，兼充消防隊總理。

translations.literal: One vice director of the vocational institute, also serving as director-general of the fire brigade.
translations.idiomatic: One vocational-institute vice director doubled as head of the fire brigade.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，五品警官五人，消防隊三人。

translations.literal: Two section chiefs, five rank-5 police officers, three for the fire brigade.
translations.idiomatic: Two section chiefs, five grade-5 police officers (three assigned to the fire brigade).

translations.literal: Two for the vocational institute.
translations.idiomatic: Two for the vocational institute.

sentences.zh: 六、七品警官各九人，消防隊各六人。

translations.literal: Nine police officers each of ranks 6 and 7; six each for the fire brigade.
translations.idiomatic: Nine grade-6 and nine grade-7 police officers; six each for the fire brigade.

translations.literal: Three each for the vocational institute.
translations.idiomatic: Three each for the vocational institute.

sentences.zh: 八、九品警官各十有二人。

translations.literal: Twelve police officers each of ranks 8 and 9.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve grade-8 and twelve grade-9 police officers.

translations.literal: Eight each for the fire brigade.
translations.idiomatic: Eight each for the fire brigade.

translations.literal: Four each for the vocational institute.
translations.idiomatic: Four each for the vocational institute.

translations.literal: All of the above were subordinate to the Police Administration Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: All of the above belonged to the Police Bureau.

translations.literal: One artisan master each of ranks 6 and 7.
translations.idiomatic: One grade-6 and one grade-7 artisan master.

translations.literal: Subordinate to the Public Works Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Public Works Bureau.

translations.literal: One medical officer each of ranks 6 and 7.
translations.idiomatic: One grade-6 and one grade-7 medical officer.

translations.literal: Subordinate to the Health Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Health Bureau.

translations.literal: From police officers downward, all were appointed by memorial to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Police officers and below were appointed by memorial.

sentences.zh: 八品錄事二十人，九品錄事三十有二人。

translations.literal: Twenty rank-8 clerks and thirty-two rank-9 clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty grade-8 and thirty-two grade-9 clerks.

translations.literal: All were appointed by consultation.
translations.idiomatic: All were appointed by consultation.

sentences.zh: 大臣掌主版籍，整飭風教，綏靖黎物，以奠邦治。

translations.literal: The minister was in charge of household registers, rectifying customs and education, pacifying the people, to secure national governance.
translations.idiomatic: The minister oversaw population registers, public morals and education, and civil order—the foundations of domestic governance.

translations.literal: The deputy minister assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy minister assisted him.

sentences.zh: 民治掌編審戶口，兼司保息鄉政。

translations.literal: Civil Administration handled household registration and review, and also managed baojia neighborhood administration.
translations.idiomatic: Civil Administration managed household registration and baojia neighborhood governance.

sentences.zh: 警政掌巡察禁令，分稽行政司法。

translations.literal: Police Administration handled patrols and prohibitions, and separately inspected administrative and judicial matters.
translations.idiomatic: Police Administration enforced patrols and bans and oversaw civil and judicial police functions.

sentences.zh: 疆裡掌經界圖志，審驗官民土地。

translations.literal: Boundaries handled boundary surveys and gazetteers, examining official and private land.
translations.idiomatic: Boundaries maintained cadastral maps and verified public and private landholdings.

sentences.zh: 營繕掌陵寢工程，修治道路，並保守古跡祠廟。

translations.literal: Public Works handled mausoleum construction, road repair, and preservation of historic sites and temples.
translations.idiomatic: Public Works maintained imperial tombs and roads and protected historic sites and temples.

sentences.zh: 衛生掌檢醫防疫，建置病院。

translations.literal: Health handled medical inspection and epidemic prevention, and establishing hospitals.
translations.idiomatic: Health managed medical inspection, epidemic prevention, and hospitals.

sentences.zh: 所轄：豫審所，後隸大理院。

translations.literal: Under its jurisdiction: the Preliminary Review Office, later subordinate to the Supreme Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: It initially oversaw the Preliminary Review Office, later transferred to the Supreme Court.

sentences.zh: 路工局，教養局，俱遴員分治之。

translations.literal: The Road Works Bureau and the Relief and Education Bureau were each administered by selected officials.
translations.idiomatic: Road works and relief/education bureaus were run by selected officials.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十年，設巡警部，置尚書，左、右侍郎，左、右丞，參議，各一人。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Guangxu the Police Ministry was established, with one minister, left and right vice ministers, left and right vice directors, and one counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 30 the Police Ministry was founded with a minister, two vice ministers, two vice directors, and a counselor.

sentences.zh: 警政、警法、警保、警學、警務五司，郎中五人，三十二年增二人。

translations.literal: Five bureaus—Police Administration, Police Law, Police Security, Police Education, and Police Affairs—with five bureau directors; two added in the thirty-second year.
translations.idiomatic: Five police bureaus began with five directors; two more were added in Guangxu 32.

sentences.zh: 員外郎、主事各十有六人，三十二年增員外郎二人，主事四人。

translations.literal: Sixteen vice directors and sixteen section chiefs each; in the thirty-second year two vice directors and four section chiefs were added.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen vice directors and sixteen section chiefs; Guangxu 32 added two vice directors and four section chiefs.

sentences.zh: 三十四年增營繕司一人。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year one Public Works Bureau director was added.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxu 34 added one public works director.

sentences.zh: 小京官四人，三十二年增五人。

translations.literal: Four junior capital officials; five added in the thirty-second year.
translations.idiomatic: Four junior capital officials, with five more in Guangxu 32.

sentences.zh: 一、二、三等書記官各十人。

translations.literal: Ten secretaries each of the first, second, and third ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Ten first-, second-, and third-rank secretaries each.

sentences.zh: 仿七、八、九品筆帖式舊制。

translations.literal: Modeled on the old system of rank 7, 8, and 9 clerks (bitieshi).
translations.idiomatic: Modeled on the old grade 7–9 clerk (bitieshi) system.

sentences.zh: 三十二年改為八、九品錄事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year changed to rank 8 and 9 record clerks (lushi).
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 32 they became grade-8 and grade-9 record clerks.

sentences.zh: 習藝所員外郎一人，主事二人。

translations.literal: One vice director and two section chiefs for the vocational institute.
translations.idiomatic: The vocational institute had one vice director and two section chiefs.

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year it was renamed the Ministry of Civil Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 32 it was renamed the Ministry of Civil Affairs.

sentences.zh: 設承政、參議兩□，置參事二人。

translations.literal: Two □ bureaus of Chancellery and Counselor were established, with two counselors (canshi) appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellery and Counselor offices were established, with two counselor-assistants.

sentences.zh: 改設民治、疆裡、營繕、衛生諸司，警政如故。

translations.literal: Bureaus for Civil Administration, Boundaries, Public Works, and Health were reorganized; Police Administration remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Civil administration, boundaries, public works, and health bureaus were reorganized; police administration unchanged.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，定習藝所及消防隊員額。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong quotas for the vocational institute and fire brigade were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1 staffing for the vocational institute and fire brigade was fixed.

translations.literal: As listed above.
translations.idiomatic: As listed above.

sentences.zh: 三年，改尚書為大臣，侍郎為副大臣。

translations.literal: In the third year ministers were renamed grand ministers and vice ministers deputy grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 3 ministers became grand ministers and vice ministers deputy grand ministers.

sentences.zh: 內、外城巡警總廳，廳丞各一人。

translations.literal: Inner and Outer City Metropolitan Police Headquarters, one bureau chief each.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner and Outer City police headquarters each had one bureau chief.

translations.literal: Originally rank 4a.
translations.idiomatic: Originally grade 4a.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十三年升從三品。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year of Guangxu promoted to sub-rank 3.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 33 the post rose to sub-grade 3.

translations.literal: Appointed by imperial selection upon request.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed by imperial selection upon request.

sentences.zh: 掌徼循坊境，並典蹕路警衛。

translations.literal: In charge of patrolling wards and districts, and also managing police escort for imperial processions.
translations.idiomatic: They patrolled wards and districts and provided police escort on imperial routes.

translations.literal: One chief secretary each for the General Affairs Office.
translations.idiomatic: Each headquarters had one chief secretary for general affairs.

translations.literal: Sub-rank 4.
translations.idiomatic: Sub-grade 4.

translations.literal: Memorial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: They were appointed by imperial memorial.

sentences.zh: 行政、司法、衛生三處各僉事三人。

translations.literal: The three offices of Administration, Judiciary, and Health each had three counselors.
translations.idiomatic: The Administration, Judiciary, and Health sections each had three fifth-rank counselors.

translations.literal: Regular fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Their rank was regular fifth grade.

translations.literal: All memorial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: All were appointed by imperial memorial.

translations.literal: Fifth-rank police officers, four each.
translations.idiomatic: There were four fifth-rank police officers at each level.

translations.literal: Sixth-rank police officers, nineteen in all.
translations.idiomatic: There were nineteen sixth-rank police officers in total.

translations.literal: Inner city ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: Ten served in the Inner City.

translations.literal: Outer city nine persons.
translations.idiomatic: Nine served in the Outer City.

translations.literal: Seventh-rank police officers twenty persons.
translations.idiomatic: There were twenty seventh-rank police officers.

translations.literal: Inner city eleven persons.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven were assigned to the Inner City.

translations.literal: Outer city nine persons.
translations.idiomatic: Nine were assigned to the Outer City.

translations.literal: Eighth-rank police officers twenty-seven persons.
translations.idiomatic: There were twenty-seven eighth-rank police officers.

translations.literal: Inner city fourteen persons.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen were assigned to the Inner City.

translations.literal: Outer city thirteen persons.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen were assigned to the Outer City.

translations.literal: Ninth-rank police officers twenty-eight persons.
translations.idiomatic: There were twenty-eight ninth-rank police officers.

translations.literal: Inner city fifteen persons.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen were assigned to the Inner City.

translations.literal: Outer city thirteen persons.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen were assigned to the Outer City.

translations.literal: Seventh rank and above, memorial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Posts of the seventh rank and above were filled by imperial memorial.

translations.literal: Eighth rank and below, consultative appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Posts of the eighth rank and below were filled by ministerial consultation.

translations.literal: Eighth- and ninth-rank record clerks, four each.
translations.idiomatic: There were four eighth-rank and four ninth-rank record clerks.

translations.literal: Delegated employment.
translations.idiomatic: They were appointed by delegation.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十年，設京師內、外城巡警總廳，置廳丞各一人。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Guangxu, the Inner and Outer City Metropolitan Patrol General Offices of the capital were established, each with one director.
translations.idiomatic: In 1904, Metropolitan Patrol general offices were set up for the Inner and Outer cities of the capital, each headed by one director.

sentences.zh: 設總務、警務、衛生三處，置參事各一人。

translations.literal: Three sections were established—General Affairs, Police Affairs, and Health—each with one counsellor.
translations.idiomatic: Three sections—General Affairs, Police Affairs, and Health—were created, each with one counsellor.

translations.literal: Regular fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The counsellors held regular fifth rank.

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year changed to counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1907 the title was changed to counselor (qian shi).

sentences.zh: 內城五分廳，外城四分廳，知事九人。

translations.literal: Inner city five branch offices, outer city four branch offices, nine directors.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner City had five branch offices and the Outer City four, with nine directors in all.

translations.literal: Regular fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The directors held regular fifth rank.

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, added a Judiciary section.
translations.idiomatic: In 1906 a Judiciary section was added.

translations.literal: Changed Police Affairs to Administration.
translations.idiomatic: Police Affairs was renamed Administration.

sentences.zh: 升總務處僉事品秩為屬官首領。

translations.literal: Raised the rank of the General Affairs section counselor to head of subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: The counselor of the General Affairs section was promoted in rank to serve as chief of the subordinate staff.

sentences.zh: 置五品以下各警官，無定員。

translations.literal: Established police officers of the fifth rank and below, without fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Police officers of the fifth rank and below were appointed without fixed quotas.

translations.literal: Eighth- and ninth-rank record clerks, four each.
translations.idiomatic: There were four eighth-rank and four ninth-rank record clerks.

sentences.zh: 並內五分廳為中、左、右三廳，外四分廳為左、右二廳，省知事四人。

translations.literal: Merged the inner five branch offices into Central, Left, and Right three offices; the outer four into Left and Right two offices; reduced four directors.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner City's five branches were consolidated into Central, Left, and Right offices; the Outer City's four into Left and Right offices; and four director posts were cut.

sentences.zh: 設內城二十六區，外城二十區，置區官、六、七品警官充。

translations.literal: Established twenty-six districts in the inner city and twenty in the outer, placing district officers filled by sixth- and seventh-rank police officers.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-six districts were set up in the Inner City and twenty in the Outer City, each headed by a district officer drawn from the sixth- and seventh-rank police ranks.

translations.literal: Soon thereafter changed to district chief.
translations.idiomatic: The title was soon changed to district chief.

translations.literal: District deputies filled by eighth- and ninth-rank police officers.
translations.idiomatic: District deputies were drawn from the eighth- and ninth-rank police officers.

translations.literal: Soon thereafter changed to district member.
translations.idiomatic: The title was soon changed to district officer.

translations.literal: One each.
translations.idiomatic: Each district had one such officer.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，省內、外城區半之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, reduced the inner and outer city districts by half.
translations.idiomatic: In 1908 the number of districts in both cities was cut by half.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，裁分廳，省知事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, abolished branch offices and cut directors.
translations.idiomatic: In 1909 the branch offices were abolished and the director posts eliminated.

sentences.zh: 度支大臣，副大臣，各一人。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue and Expenditure, vice minister, one each.
translations.idiomatic: There was one minister of revenue and expenditure and one vice minister.

sentences.zh: 左、右丞，左、右參議，各一人。

translations.literal: Left and right vice ministers, left and right counsellors, one each.
translations.idiomatic: There was one left vice minister, one right vice minister, one left counsellor, and one right counsellor.

sentences.zh: 承政、參議兩□，俱郎中三人，員外郎四人，主事三人。

translations.literal: The two □ of Executive Administration and Counselling, each with three bureau directors, four vice directors, and three section chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: The two [executive] offices of Administration and Counselling each had three bureau directors, four vice directors, and three section chiefs.

sentences.zh: 田賦、漕倉、稅課、筦榷、通阜、庫藏、廉俸、軍饟、制用、會計十司，郎中三十有一人，制用四人。

translations.literal: Ten bureaus—Land Tax, Grain Transport, Commodity Tax, Monopolies, Mining and Currency, Treasury, Salaries, Military Provisions, Disbursements, and Accounts—with thirty-one bureau directors, four in Disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: Ten bureaus—Land Tax, Grain Transport, Commodity Tax, Monopolies, Mining and Currency, Treasury, Salaries, Military Provisions, Disbursements, and Accounts—had thirty-one bureau directors in all, of whom four served in Disbursements.

translations.literal: The remainder three each.
translations.idiomatic: The other bureaus had three directors each.

sentences.zh: 員外郎四十有四人，制用六人。

translations.literal: Vice directors forty-four persons, Disbursements six persons.
translations.idiomatic: There were forty-four vice directors in all, six of them in Disbursements.

translations.literal: Land Tax and Treasury five each.
translations.idiomatic: Land Tax and Treasury each had five vice directors.

translations.literal: The remainder four each.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining bureaus had four each.

translations.literal: Section chiefs thirty-five persons.
translations.idiomatic: There were thirty-five section chiefs.

sentences.zh: 田賦、筦榷、通阜、廉俸、會計各四人，餘各三人。

translations.literal: Land Tax, Monopolies, Mining and Currency, Salaries, and Accounts four each; the remainder three each.
translations.idiomatic: Land Tax, Monopolies, Mining and Currency, Salaries, and Accounts each had four section chiefs; the other bureaus had three each.

sentences.zh: 金銀庫，郎中一人，員外郎四人，主事二人。

translations.literal: Gold and Silver Vault: one bureau director, four vice directors, two section chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: The Gold and Silver Vault had one bureau director, four vice directors, and two section chiefs.

translations.literal: Dispatch and Audit Office, changed from the Supervision and Urging Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Dispatch and Audit Office replaced the former Supervision and Urging Office.

translations.literal: One vice director, two section chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: It had one vice director and two section chiefs.

sentences.zh: 大臣掌主計算，勾會銀行幣廠，土藥統稅，以經國用。
